articles.summary: Most government digital transformation projects fail not because of bad technology, but because they optimize for launch instead of completion and treat modernization as a portal project instead of an infrastructure investment.
articles.title: Why Government Digital Transformation Projects Fail

articles.summary: When agents initiate payments, the receiving system needs more than authentication. It needs proof of who authorized the transaction, what spending authority was granted, and whether that authority is still valid.
articles.title: Who Authorized This Agent to Pay?

articles.summary: When a bank receives a mobile driver's license from another state, it needs to verify the issuer's signature. That requires trust infrastructure most banks don't have yet.
articles.title: What Does a Bank Need From a State to Verify Its mDL?

articles.summary: The Customer Identification Program rule requires banks to verify customer identity at account opening. The FinCEN ruling changes what counts as acceptable evidence.
articles.title: What Is a Customer Identification Program (CIP), and How Do Digital Credentials Change It?

articles.summary: Utah's SEDI statute prohibits architectures where the issuer can observe every credential presentation. Enforcing that requirement means choosing verification designs where the data is never generated in the first place.
articles.title: Digital Identity Without Surveillance: Understanding SEDI's No-Phone-Home Principle

articles.summary: The future of interoperable digital identity depends on more than shared formats and protocols, it depends on the governance layer that defines trust, accountability, and assurance.
articles.title: What Is a Trust Framework, and How Does It Decide Who Can Issue and Verify Digital Credentials?

articles.summary: When federal banking regulators recognize verifiable digital credentials for customer identification, digital identity stops being a government IT project and becomes financial infrastructure.
articles.title: The FinCEN Ruling Proves Digital Identity Is Financial Infrastructure

articles.summary: SEDI's Duty of Loyalty moves beyond notice and consent by establishing affirmative obligations toward individuals whose identity data is processed. It draws on academic proposals for fiduciary-like duties in privacy law.
articles.title: The SEDI Duty of Loyalty, Explained
